title: Superposition and Measurement in Quantum Mechanics
text:
A fundamental concept in quantum physics is superposition, which posits that a quantum system can exist simultaneously in multiple states until it is measured. Before observation, particles are not localized to a single position or spin; rather, they occupy a combined probability waveform describing all potential outcomes.

The process of measurement fundamentally alters the quantum state, causing the collapse of the wave function. This transition forces the system from a superposition of possibilities into a single, definite eigenstate—a phenomenon known as decoherence. This observation highlights the critical distinction between the theoretical description of reality and its empirical measurement.

Another key feature is quantum entanglement, where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate regardless of the physical distance separating them. Measuring the property of one entangled particle instantly determines the corresponding property of the other, suggesting non-local correlations that challenge classical intuitions about reality.
